strengths: Comprehensive and rigorous experimental evaluation across diverse models (LLaMA, DeBERTa, Mistral, Gemma, MoE models) and benchmarks (GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, MBPP, MT-Bench, GLUE) with 11+ baselines for NLG and 9+ for NLU
Principled problem decomposition: Breaking Catastrophic Inheritance into Knowledge Drift, Representation Collapse, and Overfitting to Noise with targeted regularizers is logical and well-motivated
Compelling controlled study (Table 3) comparing clean vs. noisy pre-training data showing 3.26-point gain on T5 vs. 1.11-point on RoBERTa—strong evidence for core hypothesis
Consistent state-of-the-art results with substantial improvements (2-3+ points) across diverse tasks and model scales (7B-70B parameters)
Thorough ablation studies, sensitivity analysis, and performance across different ranks demonstrating robustness of design choices
Thoughtful task-specific adaptations between NLU and NLG and well-justified output-space regularization strategy (Appendix D.1)
Excellent reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, implementation details, comprehensive appendix, promise of code release
Effective visualizations: t-SNE analysis (Figure 3) clearly demonstrates feature separation benefits under data imbalance
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: The three regularizers employ well-established techniques (knowledge distillation, VICReg-inspired diversity, spectral regularization); primary contribution is combining existing techniques for PEFT rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts or theoretical insights

Significant gap between problem framing and evaluation: Paper emphasizes 'bias alleviation' in abstract and title but provides no direct evaluation on fairness metrics (gender bias, stereotypes, WinoBias, StereoSet). Table 3 shows noise robustness but not bias reduction

Non-trivial computational overhead for a parameter-efficient method: Table 5 shows +10.75GB memory and +31min training time over PiSSA with limited discussion of whether practitioners would accept this trade-off for efficiency gains

Hyperparameter complexity undermines practicality: Substantially different settings for NLU vs NLG (λ₁: 0.15 vs 0.025; λ₂,λ₃: 0.03 vs 0.005), different SVD ranks (k=5 vs k=10), and unclear guidance for new tasks despite the focus on parameter efficiency

Incomplete validation of core hypothesis: Controlled study (Table 3) uses only 4 GLUE tasks and compares models with different architectures (RoBERTa vs T5), confounding corpus quality with architectural effects; would benefit from broader evaluation

Missing direct bias evaluation despite this being central to motivation: t-SNE visualization shows better feature separation but doesn't establish these features are less biased; no analysis of whether improved silhouette scores correlate with reduced demographic bias

SVD approximation unanalyzed: NLG uses randomized SVD for vocabulary-sized matrices but provides no analysis of approximation error impact; inconsistent methodology between NLU (exact SVD) and NLG (approximate SVD) lacks justification
MT-Bench underperformance unaddressed: CorDA++ maintains edge on MT-Bench (5.64 vs 5.11); lack of thorough explanation for why method doesn't consistently achieve SOTA across all benchmarks
Limited scope: Evaluation primarily on English benchmarks; no multilingual or specialized domain evaluation acknowledged in Appendix D.4 but unaddressed
Baseline comparison from original publications: While common for efficiency, scores aren't from unified experimental setup, potentially introducing confounds; acknowledged but remains a concern

strengths: Comprehensive empirical evaluation across multiple benchmarks (NLG: GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, MBPP, MT-Bench; NLU: GLUE), models (LLaMA-2, LLaMA-3, Mistral, Qwen, DeBERTa, RoBERTa, T5), and experimental settings including 10-model cross-architecture validation
Principled decomposition of Catastrophic Inheritance into three interpretable failure modes (Knowledge Drift, Representation Collapse, Overfitting to Noise) with targeted regularizers
Thorough ablation study (Table 4) demonstrating that each regularizer contributes positively; detailed hyperparameter sensitivity analysis (Figure 4)
Clever controlled study (Section 3.2.2) comparing clean (RoBERTa) vs. noisy (T5) pre-training data, providing useful insights
Practical method that is straightforward to implement and compatible with existing PEFT frameworks
weaknesses: Limited novelty: all three regularizers are well-established techniques (consistency: knowledge distillation; diversity: covariance regularization from SSL and entropy regularization; SVD: spectral regularization). The core contribution is combining existing components with PiSSA, insufficient for top-tier venue

Weak theoretical justification: the paper asserts that Knowledge Drift, Representation Collapse, and Overfitting to Noise are the root causes of Catastrophic Inheritance without rigorous justification; why output-space regularization is superior is justified intuitively but not formally; connections between failure modes and specific regularizers appear ad-hoc

Central claim about 'Catastrophic Inheritance' overstated: LoRA achieves 42.68 on GSM8K, BA-LoRA achieves 55.86—significant but not 'catastrophic'; paper conflates distinct phenomena (pre-training bias, label noise, class imbalance, overfitting) without clearly establishing which is actually problematic

Causality in Section 3.2.2 not established: the finding that BA-LoRA gains 3.26 points on noisy T5 vs. 1.11 on RoBERTa is suggestive but doesn't prove these regularizers specifically mitigate inherited noise rather than just working better generally; paper doesn't demonstrate that baseline LoRA actually exhibits the claimed failure modes

Experimental methodology concerns: baseline results sourced from other papers (Yang et al. 2025; Kang & Yin 2025) rather than uniform reimplementation, introducing uncontrolled variables; NLU/NLG use hyperparameters differing by 3-6× (λ₁: 0.025 vs. 0.15) with no justification; no statistical significance testing despite marginal improvements (e.g., 55.86±0.35 vs. 55.03±0.52)

Weak evidence for core claims: Figure 3 t-SNE visualizations show only marginal Silhouette score improvement (0.364→0.456 on balanced data); paper doesn't directly show baseline LoRA exhibits Knowledge Drift, Representation Collapse, or Overfitting to Noise or that BA-LoRA specifically addresses these
Computational cost underreported as 'modest': Table 5 shows +10.75 GB memory (16% increase) and +31 minutes (12% increase) compared to PiSSA; this is non-negligible for practitioners

Ad-hoc design choices: SVD rank selection (k=10 vs k=5) unexplained; temperature parameter (T=2.0) not justified; Top-K sampling for NLG diversity not motivated over alternatives; different regularizers for NLU vs. NLG contradicts unified framework claim

Problem definition incomplete: paper broadly defines 'Catastrophic Inheritance' but doesn't establish that it's actually a problem for LoRA fine-tuning, doesn't measure if baseline LoRA exhibits the stated failure modes, and doesn't clearly demonstrate BA-LoRA specifically addresses these phenomena rather than just being generally better regularization

strengths: Comprehensive and rigorous experimental evaluation across multiple benchmarks (NLG: GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, MBPP, MT-Bench; NLU: GLUE), models (LLaMA-2, DeBERTa, T5, RoBERTa, and diverse scales from 7B to 70B), with controlled studies comparing clean vs. noisy pre-training that directly validate the core hypothesis (3.26pt gain on T5-base vs. 1.11pt on RoBERTa-base)

Well-motivated problem formulation with clear decomposition of 'Catastrophic Inheritance' into three interpretable failure modes (Knowledge Drift, Representation Collapse, Overfitting to Noise), making the solution framework principled

Strong and consistent empirical results achieving state-of-the-art across tested benchmarks (BA-LoRA 55.86 on GSM8K, 90.67 avg GLUE), with ablations validating each component and sensitivity analysis demonstrating robustness of hyperparameter choices

Practical value with reasonable computational overhead (10.75 GB additional memory, ~31 min additional training vs. PiSSA), framework generalizability across PEFT variants (LoRA, DoRA, PiSSA), and clear implementation details supporting reproducibility

Excellent presentation with clear writing, comprehensive appendix, thoughtful design justifications (D.1-D.3), and informative visualizations including t-SNE demonstrations of improved class separation under data imbalance
weaknesses: Limited novelty: all three regularizers are established techniques (knowledge distillation from Hinton et al. 2015, covariance regularization from Bardes et al. 2021, SVD regularization from Chen et al. 2019); main contribution is combining them with PiSSA, which is primarily an engineering contribution rather than conceptual advance

Decomposition into three failure modes appears somewhat post-hoc rather than principally derived: no justification for why these three (not others) are necessary and sufficient, and connections between problems and solutions lack rigor (e.g., why specifically covariance regularization addresses representation collapse?)

Questionable baseline comparisons: sourcing different baselines from different papers with potentially different setups; the large 2.68-point average improvement (23.22→25.90) doesn't align with component improvements (0.83-1.82 points per task); extreme MBPP outlier (12-point improvement) unexplained; some error bars overlap suggesting marginal significance

Significant hyperparameter heterogeneity without sufficient justification: NLU regularization weights 6× higher than NLG (λ₁=0.15 vs 0.025); sensitivity analysis only provided for NLG; no clear guidance for practitioners on setting these for new tasks, suggesting method requires careful task-specific tuning

Key design choices lack empirical validation: no direct comparison of output-space vs. parameter-space regularization; diversity formulation choices (covariance for NLU, top-K entropy for NLG) appear ad-hoc without ablations; SVD k-value selection (10 for NLG, 5 for NLU) is arbitrary without sensitivity analysis

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across diverse NLG and NLU benchmarks with multiple model families, demonstrating consistent improvements
Well-motivated problem decomposition: Catastrophic Inheritance broken into three interpretable failure modes (Knowledge Drift, Representation Collapse, Overfitting to Noise)
Clever validation via RoBERTa vs. T5 comparison (3.26-point vs. 1.11-point gains) supporting the hypothesis that gains are larger on noisier pre-trained models
Strong interpretability through t-SNE visualizations and quantitative cluster analysis, with striking minority-class recall improvement (5.8% → 61.7%) on imbalanced data
Thorough ablation studies (Table 4) and sensitivity analysis (Figure 4) demonstrating each component contributes and robustness to hyperparameter choices
Task-aware design with validation showing covariance-based diversity is superior to entropy-based approaches for discriminative tasks (Table 11)
Excellent reproducibility: detailed hyperparameter specifications, multiple random seeds, and code release promised
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: individual regularizers (KL distillation, covariance/entropy regularization, SVD) are well-established techniques; contribution is primarily their combination for PEFT

Core hypothesis insufficiently validated: paper claims to mitigate Catastrophic Inheritance but provides no direct measurement of it; RoBERTa vs. T5 comparison is not fully controlled (differs in both architecture and pre-training objective)

Inconsistent and modest improvements across benchmarks: MT-Bench regression (5.11 vs. 5.64 for CorDA++) unexplained, largest MBPP gain (12.12) acknowledged as overfitting-prone, average gains 2.96 (NLG) and 1.20 (NLU) points
Significant computational overhead: +10.75 GB memory (+16%), +31 minutes (+18%) vs. PiSSA; O(ND²) diversity regularizer complexity concerning for large D; limited scaling analysis

Hyperparameter complexity not fully addressed: five new parameters with dramatically different values across NLU (λ₁=0.15) vs. NLG (λ₁=0.025); claims of 'simple recipe' misleading given validation-set tuning requirement

Weak theoretical justification: no principled argument for why this specific regularizer combination addresses the three failure modes; mapping between regularizers and failure modes is assumed rather than derived
Insufficient rigor in noisy pre-training hypothesis validation: uses artificial 100:10:1 imbalance, limited to MNLI, no direct measurement of inherited noise or forgetting curves during adaptation
Missing direct comparisons: no evaluation against other catastrophic inheritance mitigation approaches; no comparison to simpler regularization baselines (L2, weight decay variants)
Experimental scope limitations: English-only benchmarks, primarily 7B models, no evaluation on naturally noisy datasets, MT-Bench results rely on GPT-4 scoring (high variance) with first-turn only

SVD regularization implementation concerns: randomized SVD with large vocabularies (M × |V|) adds O(M|V|k) cost; normalization by Frobenius norm is pragmatic but less principled than singular value ratios

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across diverse models (LLaMA, Mistral, Gemma, Mixtral, DeBERTa), tasks (NLG and NLU), and scales (7B-70B), demonstrating broad applicability
Systematic ablation studies and sensitivity analyses (Table 4, Figure 4) showing clear contributions from each regularizer component with stable performance regions
Practical performance improvements with reasonable computational overhead (+31 min, +10.75GB vs PiSSA) across multiple benchmarks
Well-organized implementation details and promised code release supporting reproducibility
Thoughtful task-specific design (distinct regularizers for NLG vs NLU) showing practical understanding of domain differences
weaknesses: Core claim about 'Catastrophic Inheritance' insufficiently validated: Section 3.2.2's RoBERTa vs T5 comparison lacks proper controls (different architectures and pre-training objectives), and authors acknowledge this is not definitive evidence for the central hypothesis

Limited algorithmic novelty: all three regularizers are combinations of well-established techniques (knowledge distillation, covariance regularization from VICReg, spectral regularization). Primary contribution is combining existing methods rather than methodological innovation

Unclear whether the method addresses claimed problem vs general regularization: no comparison with adding same regularizers to full fine-tuning, and unclear why low-rank updates specifically exacerbate inherited biases rather than just constraining capacity

Weak direct evidence of bias mitigation: no evaluation on standard fairness benchmarks (WinoBias, StereoSet, BOLD), no gender/social bias analysis. Only qualitative feature visualizations and artificial MNLI class imbalance experiments

Misleading framing conflates three separate issues: generic fine-tuning overfitting (which regularization solves), representation collapse on imbalanced downstream data (which diversity helps), and amplified pre-training biases (claimed but not rigorously demonstrated)
Single fine-tuning dataset for NLG experiments (MetaMathQA-100K): generalization to other domains unclear, limiting claims about broad applicability

Non-controlled experimental design: baseline comparisons use published numbers rather than re-runs under identical hyperparameter tuning, introducing potential confounds. RoBERTa vs T5 comparison explicitly acknowledged as non-causal

Inconsistent improvements across tasks: MBPP shows 12.92-point gain over CorDA++ but MT-Bench shows minimal improvement. No analysis of when/why the method helps vs hurts, or task-specific failure modes

Hyperparameter complexity: Despite 'simple recipe' claims, requires task-specific tuning of λ₁, λ₂, λ₃ (different for NLG vs NLU), temperature T, SVD rank k, top-K value. Generalization across backbones still requires per-backbone tuning

Missing comparisons: no evaluation against other PEFT methods (Prefix-Tuning, Adapters), other bias mitigation approaches for PEFT, or data-centric alternatives. No per-step computational cost analysis

strengths: Clear problem formulation and principled decomposition of Catastrophic Inheritance into three failure modes
Exceptionally comprehensive experimental evaluation across diverse NLG/NLU tasks, model families (7B-70B), and scales with consistent improvements
Strong baselines and fair comparisons, with results directly sourced from original papers to ensure matched setups
Solid empirical evidence including RoBERTa vs. T5 comparison (3.26x larger gains on noisy T5), t-SNE visualizations with silhouette score validation, and thorough ablation studies
Task-specific regularizer design (covariance for NLU vs. entropy for NLG) with empirical validation; well-justified output-space vs. parameter-space regularization
Excellent reproducibility support: detailed hyperparameters, sensitivity analysis (Figure 4), asymptotic complexity analysis, and promised code availability
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: consistency regularizer is standard knowledge distillation, diversity regularizer replicates established covariance decorrelation (VICReg/Barlow Twins), and SVD regularizer employs established spectral regularization; main contribution is their combination for this specific problem (incremental)

Core hypothesis validation incomplete: RoBERTa vs. T5 comparison confounds three factors (corpus quality, architecture type, pre-training objective), weakening causal evidence for noise amplification claims; acknowledged as 'suggestive' by authors but not adequately addressed

Hyperparameter complexity with six main parameters (λ₁, λ₂, λ₃, k, T, K) selected via coarse grid search on validation data; risks overfitting to validation set; sensitivity analysis (Figure 4) shows non-negligible variance contradicting 'broad stability' claims
Computational overhead not negligible: +10.75 GB memory, +31 minutes training (16% slowdown) for 2-4% improvements on many tasks; cost-benefit trade-off unclear for resource-constrained settings

Fairness analysis insufficient for 'Bias-Alleviating' title: visualizations demonstrate representation quality but lack quantitative fairness metrics on protected attributes (gender, race); no demographic parity or equalized odds evaluation
Modest improvement margins (2-4% typical, some within noise margins); MT-Bench gains disproportionately small; absent statistical significance testing (no p-values or confidence intervals)

Missing scope and analysis: no multilingual or domain-specific evaluation; lacks error analysis identifying which task types benefit most; no comparison with non-PEFT bias mitigation methods; no failure case discussion

Some design choices lack strong justification: Frobenius normalization in SVD (Eq. 12) vs. alternatives unexplained; asymmetry between Top-K sampling for NLG entropy but full vocabulary for consistency loss not motivated; temperature T=2.0 chosen arbitrarily without ablation
